items.title: Federal Reserve Rate Decision Dominates Week
points: 85% probability of 25-basis-point rate hike (a 0.25% increase in the benchmark federal funds rate that banks charge each other, which filters down to consumer rates) at Wednesday's 2 p.m. ET Fed announcement.
August retail sales data releases Wednesday morning before the Fed announcement, potentially influencing final market positioning.
Fed Chair Kevin Warsh holds a 2:30 p.m. press conference, closely watched for signals on further rate increases.
The hike itself is largely priced in, so market reaction will hinge on forward guidance rather than the move itself.

items.title: Consumer Experience Sector Emerges as Growth Alternative
points: Traditional consumer discretionary stocks are losing appeal as brand loyalty weakens and products become easier to replicate; spending is shifting toward experiences like travel, events, and entertainment.
Demographic tailwinds support growth: consumers over 60 already account for a large share of global spending, with the 'silver economy' (spending by retirees and older adults) expanding rapidly.
Asset-light companies favored for capital efficiency include Live Nation, Expedia, Booking Holdings, and Airbnb.
Recent fuel price increases have pushed some Consumer Experience stocks below valuation targets, creating entry opportunities in airlines (Alaska Air, Delta) and cruise lines (Carnival, Viking).

items.title: Market Structure and Regulatory Developments
points: SEC hosts a Thursday roundtable on preparations for 24-hour trading, with major exchanges, brokers, and market makers discussing round-the-clock market access.
Bank of England announces its latest monetary policy decision Thursday, adding a data point on global rate trajectory.
Triple witching (simultaneous expiration of stock index futures, stock index options, and stock options) occurs Friday, historically driving elevated trading volume and volatility.
Notable earnings this week: Lennar (Wednesday), Carnival (Thursday), and VinFast (Friday), with housing and leisure sectors in focus amid fuel cost pressures.

items.title: iPhone Duo Launch and Specifications
points: Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo, a foldable smartphone with a passport-like design that opens and closes like a book, featuring a 5.4-inch front display expanding to a 7.6-inch interior screen for movies, games, multitasking, and work.
Starting price is $1,999 for the base model; a higher-spec variant costs over $3,100, matching pre-event analyst expectations.
The device includes Touch ID unlock and marks Apple's first entry into the foldable smartphone market.

items.title: Broader Product Ecosystem Updates
points: AirPods offer 50% improvement in noise cancellation compared to the previous generation.
iPhone 18 Pro includes 'supercharged' battery life enhancements.
The new Apple Watch can summarize ambient conversations, though an executive acknowledged potential privacy concerns about the feature.

items.title: Market Outlook and Analyst Reception
points: AT&T CEO John Stankey suggested the Duo may remain a niche product for users wanting larger devices willing to pay a premium, rather than achieving mass-market adoption.

Goldman Sachs analyst Michael Ng said the announcements were largely in line with expectations and should sustain device demand momentum, citing the foldable form factor, Touch ID on Duo, A20-series chips, and rear-camera systems.
The innovation push counters a three-year-old bear thesis that Apple lacks competitive responses to AI assistants like ChatGPT and has stalled on hardware breakthroughs.
An executive editor projects Apple shares likely higher within one year, viewing current valuation as an attractive entry point despite the Duo's potential niche status.
